quest.title: Culminate! Chatter of Joyous Dreams
quest.description: The truth is revealed! What an unpredictable turn of events!
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Invokation Coupons x100, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Friendship Eternal x2

talks.objective: Go to Caravan Ribat and find out the truth of the Card Snatcher

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we getting close? Which way should we go now?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: We just need to head a short way towards the desert. It's not far.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: I would recommend taking a bodyguard to protect you. If the customer does turn out to be rotten, you can let the bodyguard deal with them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good point! Hmm, a bodyguard...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, look! Isn't that Cyno!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Good to see you. Headed to Caravan Ribat?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Remember Paimon, we can't just disclose a customer's information...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, don't worry. This is Sumeru's General Mahamatra, Cyno. He's the leader of the Matra, and always takes criminal activity very seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Wow, how do you know so many powerful people?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Heh, you'd better get used to it Kirara. You wouldn't believe the people I've met since I started traveling with them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you have some time now, Cyno? Or do you need to go participate in the Genius Invokation tournament?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Tournament? Heh, the tournament has already finished.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Then how did you do, Cyno?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I am now the official King of Invokations.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I used Forbidden Hand at the opportune moment and drew...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Ahem. I... I can explain it later. Anyway, I have time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! Let Paimon catch you up on what's happening...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After Paimon explains for some time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon's parched now... How many times is Paimon gonna have to explain everything?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I can accompany you. As Paimon said, it's my duty to uphold the rules and punish evil.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: What do you think, Kirara?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Alright, but remember, you all should hide while I'm delivering the parcel.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: I know that this customer is suspicious, but they're still my customer until we have any concrete proof otherwise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, we'll go hide.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But if we're too far away, we won't be able to hear anything you're saying. How will we know if you're in trouble?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Not a problem, you can just watch my tails.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your tails? You mean both of them?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Of course, both of them! I'll come up with a way to have the customer confirm the contents of the package.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: If they turn out to be just an ordinary customer and the package doesn't contain the card backs, then I'll lower both of my tails. That'll mean you can just stay hidden.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: But if they turn out to be the thieves we're after, then I'll...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Lay down.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Huh? Why would she do that?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It'd be a signal, that we need to "lay down" the law...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: No way, I'm not getting on the ground, that would be way too embarrassing! Besides, don't you think that would look suspicious?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You think so? Then maybe you can use your tails to pound your back.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Uh, and why should she do that?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Simple. It'd be signal that she had "found the backs" we're looking for.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: This is the first time I've met someone as creative with their words as I am.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Have you ever considered a career in writing news headlines, Cyno?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh no, don't enable him...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Okay, if we keep standing around talking like this, the package is going to be late.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Listen to me. If they're the thieves, I'll lift one tail up and keep the other one down. If you see that, then you can come round them up.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You're not going to lay down?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: NO! I'm not laying down!

talks.objective: Go to the delivery address with Kirara

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Near the first Flaming Flower... Ah, we're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, there aren't any houses around here.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Maybe the recipient planned on coming here to personally receive the package. I've had customers do that in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: We're still a little early. In the meantime, why don't the rest of you go find a place to hide?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: And remember, watch my tails for the signal!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: We'll hide here. This spot is hidden, but with a clear view.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sure this recipient's up to no good! Who'd pick up a package in a place like this!?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I agree.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: But for the sake of her company's reputation, we'll let her "tail" us what to do.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What? As in her "tails"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah yeah, we get it...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After waiting behind the rocks for a while...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, look! Someone's coming!

dialogues.speaker: Recipient
dialogues.text: You from Komaniya Express?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: That's right. You must be Mr. Dedebaba?

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: Where's the package?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ah yes, this is your package. Here you go.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I recommend that you open it and confirm the contents. I've been running to many places the past few days through all sorts of weather. The contents may have shifted, so it's best to check that everything's intact.

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: No need. You haven't opened it to see what's inside, have you?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Of course not. That would be against our company policy.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: But if the contents are valuable, I would still recommend checking them first. If anything turns out to be damaged, I could compensate you now.

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: I said no need, didn't I? Why are you so persistent?

dialogues.speaker: Pabag
dialogues.text: You know, Boss... This little lady's out here all on her own.

dialogues.speaker: Papak
dialogues.text: We could use that to our advantage, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: Hey, you. Are you the only one delivering out here?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Huh? Uh, y—yes, that's right... I wouldn't bring a bunch of people with me to deliver a package.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: (Uh oh! I'm no good at lying! And I can't keep my tails from moving everywhere!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, she's giving a signal!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But wait... Uh, Paimon doesn't recognize that signal at all.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Ah, I nearly forgot... Th—This just happens to be my 100th delivery. It's a really special moment for me!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: If you could let me know what I delivered, it would mean a lot to me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Her tails are moving all over the place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does she need us to step in or not?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Her tails keep moving and intertwining... They keep pointing in different directions...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ah! Maybe she's trying to say that she mixed up her directions! These people aren't the intended recipients!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seriously!? There's no way anyone could get all that from just her tails!

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: Something's not right... I can feel it. And you seem real concerned about this package, missy.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Oh, hehe, no... That's just part of my job, we always care about the customer! Are you really not going to open it?

dialogues.speaker: Pabag
dialogues.text: C'mon Boss, enough talk!

dialogues.speaker: Papak
dialogues.text: Yeah, nobody will ever know anything happened way out here!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Uh, th—then do you have a moment to leave a five-star review?

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: Hmph, sure. I'll leave a five-star review... after you're dead!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! They've got a knife! Forget the signals!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've gotta save Kirara!

dialogues.speaker: Pabag
dialogues.text: Boss! She's got backup!

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: What are ya afraid of!? Get 'em!

dialogues.speaker: Papak
dialogues.text: Huh? Wait, th—that's Cyno! The General Mahamatra!

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: C—Cyno!?

talks.objective: Talk to the recipient of the package

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kirara, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yeah, I'm fine. Don't worry.

dialogues.speaker: Dedebaba
dialogues.text: Had I known you were here, we wouldn't have...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Too late for that. And I don't want to hear any whining from you two, either. Clear?

dialogues.speaker: Pabag
dialogues.text: Y—Yes... C—Crystal clear!

dialogues.speaker: Papak
dialogues.text: General Mahamatra, I—I don't want to go to prison... Can't you just let us off this one time?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: That depends on how honest you are.

dialogues.speaker: Papak
dialogues.text: We'll tell you everything!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What's inside the package?

dialogues.speaker: Papak
dialogues.text: Card backs... Genius Invokation TCG card backs that we collected from different nations.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are they the kind with a treasure chest design on them?

dialogues.speaker: Pabag
dialogues.text: Y—Yeah, that's right! Wait, how'd you know that?

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: W—We're just a group of Treasure Hoarders, that's all...

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: Some hoarders were getting fed up recently with just stealing small stuff. They wanted to, uh...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Go on.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: They wanted to pull off something big... You know, not just in one nation, all across Teyvat!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All across Teyvat?

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: Yeah, we were planning to steal prized treasures from different nations all at the same time.

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: After pulling off a job like that, everyone would recognize us Treasure Hoarders as the most powerful organization across the world!

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: But, uh... seems like that's not gonna happen now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what does any of that have to do with these card backs?

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: Well, the problem was we didn't know how to communicate our master plan to all the other Treasure Hoarders.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: But with how popular Genius Invokation TCG has become recently, somebody suddenly came up with the idea to use cards as a way to communicate our plans without being detected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you were the ones who printed these card backs.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: Yeah... Because every Treasure Hoarder knows what to do once they see a treasure chest.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: First you bury it, so no one else can take it. Then just add a little bit of...

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: Hey, shut it! You're givin' away all our plans...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: It appears you consider this ridiculous plan of yours more valuable than your own life.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: Ahh! N—No, no, no! I'll talk, I'll talk...

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: All you need to do is cover it with some wet dirt or sand, then wipe it off after a while...

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: And it'll look like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "My fellow hoarders, this is the big job we've all been waiting for. Take up your daggers, put on your masks, and round up your Sumpter Beasts..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Oh, and for those of you without Sumpter Beasts..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously, that's all it says? What a waste!

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: Hey, whaddya mean "waste"!? That message will mobilize the Treasure Hoarders!

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: H—He's right, the time and other details are printed below that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Oh, there it is!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Hmm, objectively speaking, it's definitely a creative method of communicating information.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But then why were you trying to retrieve these card backs?

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: It's all because some fellow hoarders got addicted to Genius Invokation!

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: All they needed to do was stick to the plan, but they couldn't help themselves and started playing the game! Not only that, they were even using our card backs and showing 'em off!

response.speaker: Pabag
response.text: But that wasn't the worst of it, some of them ended up losing our card backs to other players.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Ah, you were afraid that your plans would be exposed, so you dispatched members to quickly retrieve the card backs that had been scattered into the markets.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: Not just the ones on the markets, we collected ALL our treasure chest card backs and we had them shipped back.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: We feared that our plans had already been discovered, so we were preparing to print another set of card backs. They would indicate a different time to initiate the operation, and we'd redistribute them...

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: But to take every precaution, we raised funding for everyone to send us the backs via Komaniya Express. That way, we could guarantee the card backs would arrive safely and on time.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Huh? Oh, uh thanks for the compliments...

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: So the senders would stay at their original location to ensure that the operation could continue moving forward.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Now that I think about it, that must be why the Treasure Hoarders came after the person who sold the card back in Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! It's no wonder we were running into the Treasure Hoarders left and right. They wanted to be sure that anyone involved stayed quiet.

response.speaker: Papak
response.text: There, I told you everything I know. Hopefully that will help us make up for our mistakes... Please, Mahamatra Cyno, show us mercy!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You'll each receive your due punishment. Enough talk, come with me.

choices.text: And why are you stealing card backs?

talks.objective: Talk to Cyno in Caravan Ribat

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You follow Cyno back to Caravan Ribat...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I've taken care of the criminals for now. I'll be escorting them back to Sumeru City shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for all your help.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I was only fulfilling my duty. You all did well.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: (Cyno seems like a completely different person when he's working.)

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright, goodbye for now.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, wait wait wait! I still wanna interview the champion of the Sumeru regional tournament.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Alright, go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Tell me, Mr. Cyno, what were your thoughts about the tournament? And did you have anything to say about the Treasure Hoarder incident?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Genius Invokation TCG is a very good game. But to me, it's not just a game, it's an art form. It allows people to meet others, make friends, and experience the joy of dueling together.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I hope everyone can have the chance to experience the fun of playing this game.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Great answer. That'll be a perfect ending for my news piece.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Therefore, I assure you that I will personally bring judgment to any criminals out there with delusions of desecrating this game with their evil plans. No matter where you run, or where you hide, you will not escape the punishment of lightning.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh! Ahem, I see... Let's stay calm, no need to get worked up.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Now let me think...

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Hmm... "Not-So-Genius Thieves Behind Mysterious Treasure-Chest Card Back Plot Finally"... umm...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: "Got decked..." You get it, like cards and punching?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Yes, that'll work nicely!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These two make quite the team when it comes to words.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: If that's all, then I should get going.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'll inform the other areas not to get gamed by these thieving Treasure Hoarders.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: We will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So in the end, it turned out that the group of card snatchers we were tracking was the Treasure Hoarders all along.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still feels a little disappointing though... Paimon thought for sure those card backs would lead us to some valuable treasure.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Don't say that. Think of the bright side, we uncovered a major international crime scheme!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I definitely have everything I need for my exclusive news piece.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If anything, Paimon regrets that we didn't get to see the mysterious inventors of Genius Invokation TCG.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Hehe, it seems everyone can't stop talking about that game.

choices.text: It's just fun to play cards.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: In that case, how would everyone like to join me for a very special delivery?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You mean it's related to Genius Invokation TCG?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Mm-hmm, that's right. You'll understand when we get there.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: I would have invited Cyno along too if he wasn't busy with work.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Oh really? But didn't you say before that you can't disclose customer information?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Yeah, but this time the situation's different.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Let's just say, this delivery wasn't assigned to me by the company.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: This package had been sitting at the company for some time because we couldn't ever locate the recipient. Even the neighbors didn't know where he went.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so the company eventually took ownership of the package?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Yep, the holding period passed just last month.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: But can't you just return it to the original sender?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Well, it turns out the sender has passed away.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's terrible...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Yeah, and I thought both the original sender and intended recipient would be disappointed if this package is left undelivered.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: So I took the initiative and started asking around Sumeru in my free time. Eventually, I found out where the recipient went, and also learned a little about his past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, amazing! So who is it?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Well... Hehe, you'll have to come with me and see.

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: I have a feeling that it'll be good to have some true Genius Invokation TCG players like you come along.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Oh, sounds like another news story brewing. I'll tag along, as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, now Paimon's really curious...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Shall we join her?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Alright, then follow me to Vimara Village.

choices.text: It's our duty as TCG players.
It's fun to meet new friends.
Let's play a game of Genius Invokation next time.

talks.objective: Go to Vimara Village to deliver the package

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: The clues pointed to Vimara Village, but I'm not sure of which house they live in exactly.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Guess we'll have to ask around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Any idea what the recipient looks like?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: I only know his name is Garvipidam, and that he's a scholar from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Garvipidam... got it.

talks.objective: Ask Zadith about the whereabouts of the scholar

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there, do you know where Garvipidam lives?

dialogues.speaker: Zadith
dialogues.text: Hmm, I'm afraid I've never heard that name before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's a scholar from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Zadith
dialogues.text: Oh, yes, there is a scholar around here, but I've never heard anyone go by the name you mentioned.

dialogues.speaker: Zadith
dialogues.text: Are you sure you've got the right name? Actually, I'd like to ask him a few questions myself regarding which of the Six Darshans to join!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, sounds like he doesn't know. Let's go ask someone else.

talks.objective: Ask Arezo about the whereabouts of the scholar

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, we're looking for a scholar named Garvipidam.

dialogues.speaker: Arezo
dialogues.text: Garvipidam? Never heard of 'em.

dialogues.speaker: Arezo
dialogues.text: Ah, wait. Do you mean that newcomer that arrived a few days ago?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, someone just moved here?

dialogues.speaker: Arezo
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right. He looked pretty anxious though, almost like he's struggling to complete a thesis.

dialogues.speaker: Arezo
dialogues.text: I've seen him speaking with the village head, probably looking for a place to stay.

dialogues.speaker: Arezo
dialogues.text: Vimara Village is the perfect place to take a vacation and relax, which is why I chose to come back here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it, thank you. We'll go talk to the head of the village.

dialogues.speaker: Arezo
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. If life is ever treatin' ya hard, you can always come and live here for a while.

talks.objective: Ask the village head about the whereabouts of the scholar

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, are you the head of the village? There's something we'd like to ask you about.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Yes, that's me. Go ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you know where a scholar by the name of Garvipidam lives? We'd like to talk to him.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Garvipidam? Ah, that must be him...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know him?

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Yes, I do. He came here to rent a place to stay. He said he needed to unwind a little.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: But hardly anyone's ever seen him come out since he moved in, he doesn't seem to be very outgoing.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: I don't know if that's his way of "unwinding," but I'd say he's just keeping himself cooped up.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Are you friends of his?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yeah, you could say that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Hmm? Her tails are moving again. Is that what happens whenever she tells a lie?)

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Ah, I see. I was thinking that it'd be good for some friends to check up on him.

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: He's staying up above, look for the house in the corner. You should be able to find him there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great, thank you very much!

dialogues.speaker: Amadhiah
dialogues.text: Don't mention it. I just want to see people who come here be happy.

talks.objective: Go to the house and talk to Garvipidam

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the place. Let's try knocking and see if he answers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello? Anybody home? We're looking for Garvipidam.

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: Yes, that's me. Can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Hello Mr. Garvipidam, I'm Kirara. I have a delivery from Komaniya Express... I'm afraid the package is quite late.

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: A package? For me?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yes, it's from a Mr. Gulab.

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: Wh—What? Gulab? But how is that possible...

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Yes, it seems your friend submitted the package to our company before he passed.

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: Friend? Hah, some friend I am... There was nothing I could do about his illness, and I wasn't by his side during the last moments of his life.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Don't say that. After all, you and Gulab are the creators of Genius Invokation TCG. I'm sure Gulab would have been happy to know how popular the game has become.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Say what!? He's one of the creators of Genius Invokation TCG!?

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: *sigh* Why... Why does it seem that misfortune always befalls geniuses like him?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: If you don't mind, perhaps you could talk to us about it? It would probably help you feel better.

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: Hah, you're right. Maybe I should tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Garvipidam
dialogues.text: You really wouldn't mind listening?

choices.text: Sure, you can talk to us.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Alright then... It's not much of a story, really.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: I knew Gulab ever since we were kids. We were classmates and grew up together.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Other than the bandages on his arms, you could hardly tell he had Eleazar. He was always positive, peaceful, and kind...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Later, we both entered the Akademiya, and he became a Rtawahist Dastur.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: If I remember correctly, that's a pretty high position.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Haha. Yes, he really was that smart.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: But before long, the Eleazar got worse and led to some serious complications.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: After that, he became bedridden. He received treatment in the hospital, but had to abandon his research.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: I would go see him in the hospital every day, even though he said there was no need for me to visit so often.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: He must have been worried that he was taking time from your own research.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: I know, but I couldn't bear to just leave him like that. He was clearly the smarter of the two of us.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: We would have some free time whenever I visited him, so we took some cards and started painting them.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Over time, those cards became the basis for Genius Invokation TCG.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: A game that was born from friendship.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: It's not only a game. When we were designing it, I deliberately incorporated some theoretical knowledge of the elements.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: I was originally waiting for him to recover, so we could study the subject together. But in the end...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, don't be sad. Genius Invokation TCG is the result of your research together.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not to mention, a lot of people are enjoying it now.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: *sigh* After he passed away, I tried to play the game with someone else...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: But every time I looked up, all I could see was his silhouette. It was as if he was still sitting there at the table...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: I know it was all in my head, though...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Aw, Paimon understands. Paimon wouldn't ever be able to get used to being away from {NICKNAME}. Paimon would probably find herself talking to the wind as if the Traveler could hear...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Yes. Everyone else has told me that I have to move on and embrace the fun of Genius Invokation, saying that I'm one of its creators...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: But to be honest, without Gulab, what meaning does the game have anymore...?

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: Garvipidam, perhaps you should see what your friend sent you in the package.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Ah, right.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Hmm!? What's this? ...A letter?

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Gulab... that rascal... He was always this way...

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: I haven't played much Genius Invokation myself. All I know is that it has brought joy to a lot of people.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: As a true TCG player put it: "The game allows many people to meet others, make friends, and experience the joy of dueling together."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! We've seen that firsthand on our journeys recently!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can tell you those stories if you're interested.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Thank you all for your kind words.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: You're right.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: Haha, Gulab... Is that what you were thinking when you left this letter...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: I've always kept your Casket of Tomes with me...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: It was so special for you to draw me a card like this, what a waste it is to never have used it...

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: If he were here now, I know he'd say.

response.speaker: Garvipidam
response.text: "Hey friends, how about a game of Genius Invokation TCG?" Well, what do you say?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd be happy to.

choices.text: They stay with us in another form.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Garvipidam seems to be feeling better. Paimon even saw him crack a smile when he was playing just now.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: It always takes time to heal from pain from the past, but I think this is a good start for his road to recovery.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! It was a good thing that Kirara kept track of that package, even when they were unable to deliver it.

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: When my boss asked me to take care of it, I had a feeling that it must somehow be delivered, I couldn't just let it be abandoned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Would you say that was your youkai intuition kicking in?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Maybe, I'm not sure. I guess I just didn't want to let the sender's sentiment go to waste like that.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Anyway, I think this is where we'll say goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, are you going back to Fontaine now?

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: That's right. Who would have guessed that I'd still get such a quality story after the tournament had finished. It's going to take me a few days just to draft the articles alone.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: Oh, by the way, I still haven't had the chance to interview you two all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Charlotte
dialogues.text: After all that we've witnessed on this journey together, do you have anything you'd like to say?

choices.text: We made a lot of new friends...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You could say the best thing we got out of this adventure was the new friends we made!

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: I understand. I'll be sure to work your comments into my exclusive news piece.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Just be sure to buy a copy of The Steambird when you visit Fontaine!

response.speaker: Kirara
response.text: And I should get ready to head back to Inazuma. I still have to report everything to my boss.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Take care, everyone.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: Will do! I'm sure we'll all see each other again soon.

response.speaker: Charlotte
response.text: And maybe we'll play Genius Invokation TCG if we have the chance.

choices.text: We learned a lot about Genius Invokation TCG...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! We'll never see the game the same way, it means a lot more to us now!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: The customer will be here soon, so be sure to stay out of sight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're in the middle of nowhere, though. Are you sure this is the right place, Kirara?

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: Let's see, the address is, "Approximately 100 paces down the road from Caravan Ribat towards the desert, near the first Flaming Flower."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's the most suspicious address Paimon's ever heard!

dialogues.speaker: Kirara
dialogues.text: (Meow...)
